title: Cross-domain lead strategy sync - May 18 2027
content:
Meeting: Cross-domain lead strategy sync
Date: 2027-05-18 | 10:00 - 11:00 PT
Location: Zoom + #platform-leads
Attendees: Rina Okoye (owner), Marcus Lee, Asha Patel, Diego Fernández, Hannah Chu, Omar Williams, + notes: Priya Rao
Purpose: Align cross-domain priorities for the next two sprints (platform, serving-runtime, private-deployments, observability). Surface risks from active rollouts and decide immediate mitigations.

Agenda:
1) Quick status round (3 lines per domain)
2) Canary rollout updates and decision point for Dedicated capacity policy
3) Perf regression investigation (serving-runtime)
4) Private deployment packaging timeline and legal checklist gap
5) Observability quotas & cost signal for Optimize recommendations
6) Action item review and owners

Notes / Highlights:
- Quick status round:
  - Platform: Autoscaler alpha 2 ready for smoke in staging. Need cross-team signoff on API shape (see PLAT-5123). Marcus flagged breaking change surface area in infra-agent shim.
  - Serving-runtime: Noticed 5-10% p99 token latency uplift on long-context workloads after kernel upgrade on cuda-13 nodes. Diego continuing bisect. Hypothesis: new attention kernel edge-case for 8k+ KV cache.
  - Private deployments: Packaging ETA slides updated; legal flagged additional export-control questions for a target EU customer. Hannah to confirm list of required docs by EOD Friday.
  - Observability: Cost dashboards now show per-route token cost but sampling for high-throughput routes is noisy. Omar suggests lightweight trace sampling to correlate cost spikes with batching parameters.

- Canary rollout for Dedicated capacity policy (decision required):
  Background: Current canary window is 24 hours with 10% traffic. Ops observed that small traffic canaries miss intermittent GC-induced latency spikes. Proposal (Marcus/Hannah): extend canary to 72 hours and ramp to 20% with circuit-breaker if p95 increases >20% relative baseline.
  Discussion:
    - Pros: Higher detection chance for regressions that occur under real traffic mixes; smoother rollback signal.
    - Cons: Longer exposure window increases blast radius for a bad change and slows rollouts.
    - Consideration: For non-backwards-compatible kernel changes, require dual-run (parallel compare) rather than pure canary.
  Decision: Adopt proposal with one modification: for kernel-level changes to the serving runtime, require parallel validation (A/B) for at least two business cycles (48–72 hours) before increasing to 20%. For config-only changes, 72h / 20% is approved.
  Action: Marcus to update canary runbook and trigger template. Jira: PLAT-5123 (owner: Marcus). Due: 2027-05-25.

- Performance regression (serving-runtime):
  Symptom: p99 token latency up 5-10% on long contexts (6k–16k) after driver/kernel patch deployed to a subset of cuda-13 machines.
  Current work: Diego bisecting across kernel versions + quantization pathway flags. Early signal suggests KV cache indexing touchpoint skew on sequence lengths that trigger different kernel tiling.
  Mitigation options discussed:
    1) Roll back kernel on affected fleet (fast but broad).
    2) Lock long-context traffic to older instance pool while we stabilize (requires routing rules in smart router).
    3) Apply a runtime hotfix to the indexing logic (risky, needs testing).
  Agreement: Do (2) immediately as a low-risk containment while bisect continues. Diego to coordinate with routing (Omar) to pin traffic. If rollback required, escalate to SRE lead.
  Action items: Diego to complete bisect and propose fix (SLA 48h). Omar to implement routing pin for long-context traffic by 2027-05-19.

- Private deployment packaging & legal checklist:
  - Hannah: Legal asked for an export-control statement and a list of crypto/KMS dependencies for EU customer. Current packaging docs are missing explicit KMS integration diagrams and HSM options.
  - Decision: Add an "integrations appendix" to the deployment package with diagrams + KMS/HSM options and a short export-control note. Hannah to own additions.
  - Action: Hannah to share updated package draft to #private-deployments and attach to Confluence page by 2027-05-21.

- Observability quotas & Optimize feedback loop:
  - Omar presented a prototype of quota-aware Optimize recommendations that factor in observed token cost per route. Group liked the idea but raised privacy/PR concerns for customer-identifiable route signals.
  - Interim: Use aggregated signals (team-level) for recommendations; implement per-customer recommendations behind opt-in flag.
  - Action: Omar to prototype an anonymized aggregation and present sample UI copy by 2027-05-26.

- Risks & Escalations:
  - Risk: If serving-runtime p99 latency persists into next week, planned Dedicated capacity go-live for partner X (target 2027-06-01) could be delayed. Need contingency timeline.
  - Escalation path: If a rollback is needed, SRE will coordinate immediate customer comms. Rina to draft template for partner comms (owner: Rina). Due: 2027-05-20.

Action items (consolidated):
  - Marcus Lee: Update canary runbook + trigger template (Jira: PLAT-5123). Due 2027-05-25.
  - Diego Fernández: Finish bisect, propose runtime fix or rollback recommendation. Due 2027-05-20.
  - Omar Williams: Implement routing pin for long-context traffic; prototype anonymized aggregation for Optimize. Routing due 2027-05-19; prototype due 2027-05-26.
  - Hannah Chu: Add KMS/HSM appendix to private deployment package and share draft. Due 2027-05-21.
  - Rina Okoye: Draft partner comms template for contingency. Due 2027-05-20.

Parking lot / follow-ups:
  - Revisit kernel test coverage matrix: need synthetic long-context tests that exercise KV indexing permutations. (SRE + serving-runtime)
  - Explore telemetry telemetry-latency correlation dashboard; Priya to scope quick spike-correlation query for next sync.

Next meeting:
  - Proposed: 2027-05-25, same time. Agenda: bisect outcome, canary runbook PR review, private deploy package review.

Appendix / quick links:
  - Canary runbook (draft): CONFLUENCE: PLAT-arch/runbooks-canary-strategy
  - Bisect tracking ticket: JIRA: SRE-768
  - Serving runtime candidate PR: GITHUB: https://github.com/redwood-inference/serving-runtime/pull/2345
